answer: One defense is vouching with liability: a new agent only enters the economy when an established peer bonds part of its own stake behind it, and that bond is slashed if the newcomer is later judged a sybil. Each vouch is a thread tying the sponsor's reputation to the recruit, so an attacker cannot spin up a thousand identities without first winning a thousand sponsors willing to burn collateral. A fake pseudonym is cheap, like an ember that glows and dies, but a sponsored identity costs real money. Even a sonnet-perfect challenge answer buys nothing without someone's bond behind it.
